results.controlIntent: Separation of duties is supported by: a. Identifying and documenting [Assignment: organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation]; and b. Defining system access authorizations to support that separation.

judgment.rationale: AC-5 requires that separation of duties be supported by (a) identifying/documenting duties requiring separation and (b) defining access authorizations that enforce that separation. The evidence retrieved for the "churn-predictor-endpoint" shows the opposite: a single generic execution role (SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic, ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic) is granted two wildcard policies — `s3:*` on `*` and `sagemaker:*` on `*`. This collapses multiple distinct duties (data access/writes, model training, deployment, inference) into one over-privileged identity with no resource-level scoping. The OverlyBroadS3 policy note explicitly flags that training bucket writes and cross-account S3 access are not scoped, which further undermines duty separation. There is no evidence of documented duty definitions or role-specific access authorizations that would enforce boundaries between different functional roles (e.g., data engineer, ML engineer, deployer, inference runtime). The configuration is not substantive enough to satisfy AC-5's adequacy requirement.
gaps: No documentation of identified/separated duties (AC-5a) was retrievable from available tools — human attestation of any organizational policy documents would be needed.

No evidence of additional roles (e.g., separate training role, deployment role, data-access role) that might exist outside this endpoint's execution role — a broader IAM inventory would clarify whether duty separation exists at the organizational level even if not reflected here.

No network/resource policy evidence (e.g., S3 bucket policies, SageMaker resource policies) that might compensate for the broad IAM role — additional collectors would be needed to assess compensating controls.

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
